title: How telecoms upgrade work sparked US flight chaos
excerpt: US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading and not a cyber-attack.
summary: As it swapped out copper lines for fibre at a remote location in the US, L3Harris installed a router - a piece of equipment which basically directs traffic across the network. Juliette Kayyem, US assistant secretary of Homeland Security under President Barack Obama, questioned why an upgrade was done on one of the week's busiest days for travel. A spokesperson for L3Harris said is it "supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the 13 November ground stop of our nation's air travel".

title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
excerpt: Fully automated ransomware hasn’t arrived—yet. But seemingly unsophisticated attackers are using AI tools to wreak havoc.
summary: But in the new era of AI-powered and automated cyberattacks, the danger posed by ransomware is only increasing as cybercriminals profit by combining established methods with new techniques made possible or more accessible by AI. Kaiser notes that broader trends in scamming are always relevant to ransomware, because attackers often use the same types of phishing and social engineering techniques to gain initial access to targeted systems. In Japan, for example, successful scamming has spiked drastically in recent months as AI enables foreign attackers to generate consistently convincing content in Japanese for the first time.

title: Uber confirms hackers stole thousands of drivers’ license information in data breach
excerpt: The ridesharing giant said drivers' license information stored by AI cloud company Fireworks AI was stolen during a security incident.
summary: In notices filed this week with several U.S. attorneys general, including California, the ride-hail giant said it was notified on October 9 by the provider that hackers broke in and stole internal credentials, which were used to access Uber’s data. Fireworks attributed its breach to a financially motivated cybercriminal group whose goals are to sell stolen tokens for accessing large language models, or LLMs. The company reported a security incident at its Uber Freight truck shipping unit, for which an extortion gang took credit for stealing data.

title: This week in science: PTSD prediction, phishing while tired, an exoplanet

title: United Airlines blocks AI agents from booking flights, citing cybersecurity risks
excerpt: The airline said it will not allow customers to use AI agents to book flights and manage reservations.
summary: United Airlines said it will restrict access to AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on their users’ behalf, citing a risk to cybersecurity and undermining federal regulations. The airline also warns of a risk of violating federal aviation rules, such as requiring that a human completes flight check-ins to acknowledge that their bags do not contain banned substances. “As a result, United is taking steps to restrict access — directly within our digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators — to prohibit use by unauthorized, third-party personal AI agents or assistants,” the airline said in a statement.
